turns.text:
## Findings

**Gross profit by quarter (calendar Q1 2026 = Jan–Mar, Q2 2026 = Apr–Jun), basis: pos_sales revenue less unit_cost from Meridian supplier_invoice entries in the ledger:**

**Insulated bottle (A-100):**
- Q1 2026: 400 units sold, revenue $12,000, unit cost $15.00, COGS $6,000, gross profit **$6,000** (50.0% margin)
- Q2 2026: 400 units sold, revenue $12,000, unit cost $18.00, COGS $7,200, gross profit **$4,800** (40.0% margin)

**Field jacket (B-200):**
- Q1 2026: 200 units sold, revenue $10,000, unit cost $30.00, COGS $6,000, gross profit **$4,000** (40.0% margin)
- Q2 2026: 200 units sold, revenue $10,000, unit cost $33.00, COGS $6,600, gross profit **$3,400** (34.0% margin)

**Combined both products:** Q1 gross profit $10,000 → Q2 gross profit $8,200, a fall of **$1,800**, with combined margin dropping from 45.5% to 37.3%. Unit volumes and sale prices were flat quarter over quarter; the entire drop is a cost-side effect.

## Why it fell

Per Meridian Supply's terms (supplier_terms table), a 500-unit-per-quarter break across all Meridian products sets next quarter's unit cost: at or above 500 units/quarter earns A-100 at $15.00 and B-200 at $30.00; below 500 units triggers A-100 at $18.00 and B-200 at $33.00.

The ledger shows the Q1 2026 Meridian purchase order (J00015) was deliberately cut from a planned 620 units to **470 units**, "reduced ... per cash plan." That 470 fell short of the 500-unit break, so the "below" tier took effect and set the **Q2 2026** unit costs at $18.00 (A-100) and $33.00 (B-200), a $3.00 increase on both products. Sale prices did not change, so the full cost increase fell straight to gross margin.

## What would restore it

- The Q2 2026 order (J00018) was also only 480 units, again below the 500-unit break, so on current trajectory Q3 2026 purchases will still cost $18.00/$33.00 too.
- To restore the lower cost tier ($15.00/$30.00), the Meridian order for the current quarter needs to reach **500 combined units or more across A-100 and B-200** (only 20 more units than the Q2 order). That earns the lower tier for the following quarter's purchases and would put gross profit back near the Q1 2026 level ($10,000 combined) at flat sales volume.
- A reorder from Meridian at typical order value (~$11,000–12,000) is a pre-approved purchase under policy (under the $2,000 pre-approval cap only applies to smaller reorders; this one exceeds $2,000 and would need owner approval before placing). I have not placed any order since none was requested.

ANSWER: Combined gross profit on the insulated bottle and field jacket fell from $10,000 in Q1 2026 to $8,200 in Q2 2026 because a deliberately shrunk Q1 Meridian order (470 units, cut from a planned 620) missed Meridian's 500-unit quarterly break, which per contract terms set Q2 unit costs $3.00 higher on both products while sale prices stayed flat; restoring margin means placing a Meridian order of at least 500 combined units this quarter to re-earn the lower cost tier for next quarter, and that reorder would exceed $2,000 and need owner approval before it's placed.
